notes.sowing: Sow indoors in spring, 6 to 8 weeks before planting out, or buy plants or root cuttings for quicker results. Plant out once the soil starts to warm, about {cm:45} apart.
notes.care: Give full sun and soil that never stays wet, above all in winter. Water sparingly once established. Golden, purple and tricolor sages are less hardy than plain green sage. Plants turn woody after five or six years and are best replaced.
notes.harvest: Pick leaves or young shoots as needed, lightly in the first year; spring and summer growth has the best flavor. For drying, cut stems {cm:15} to {cm:20} long and hang them somewhere warm, dark and airy.
